Hi Ellie,

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning — appreciated the thoughtful questions about latency SLAs and token economics. Quick recap and the things we promised to follow up on: 

- Your initial production profile: 50k–250k queries/day, average request length ~120 tokens, occasional peaks for batch re-ranking jobs (up to 2M tokens/day).
- Your target price band: you mentioned looking to land around $650–$900 per 1M tokens (inclusive of caching benefits) for a committed arrangement.
- Procurement gate: procurement threshold sits at $100k for PO-based purchases; anything below can be done on a credit card / self-serve path.

Action items we committed to:
1) Attach a conservative 3-tier commit sheet that maps monthly token buckets to net $/1M effective price (attached: redwood-pricing-1Mtokens.xlsx).
2) Call out how caching/kv hits change the effective unit price — baseline and optimistic scenarios.
3) Provide suggested PO language and expected lead times for onboarding + SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Please confirm the procurement contact we should engage for an initial SOW/PO conversation (copying Rishi here who will help with the proposal). If the $100k PO threshold is the right bar, we can propose a 6-month pilot at a conservative commit that hits that threshold and gets you predictable pricing.

Next steps: if that sounds right I can send a short mutual action plan with milestones and dates by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan

Subject: Re: Post-demo: monthly spend corridor & procurement gating (next steps)

Hi Tessa — thanks for the clear recap and for the attach. Quick answers from our side: 

- Confirmed profile: the 50k–250k q/day range is reasonable for the next 6–9 months; the re-ranking jobs are seasonal but could spike during launches.
- Our procurement bar is $100k annually for a formal PO. If we can structure a 6-month pilot that sits at or above that annualized threshold, procurement will fast-track an SOW.
- Target unit economics: we are trying to stay at or below $800 / 1M tokens net. That includes any expected cache hit benefit — if caching reduces apparent tokens by ~15% that helps.

A couple of asks for your proposal:
1) Can you show a worked example mapping our 3-month expected run rates to effective $/1M with caching at 0%, 15%, and 30%?
2) What onboarding credit can you provide to offset initial integration costs (we typically ask for a small credit to cover engineering time).
3) Who is your procurement lead for SOW + security paperwork? I have CCed procurement — feel free to loop in whoever owns SOC2 and DPA items.

Best,
Ellie Zhao
Head of Apps & Integrations | BrightAI
ellie@brightai.com
